title: Choosing a thinning method
text: zhang_suen default matches EBImage::thinImage() behavior. thinImage() wrapper provided drop-replacement. lee 2-D adaptation Lee’s original 3-D algorithm. 3-D case (volumetric thinning) implemented release. K3M lookup tables implementation reconstructed algorithm’s published description; produce topology-preserving, one-pixel-wide skeletons test corpus. Verification paper’s exact tables welcomed.

title: Choosing a thinning method
text: four algorithms produce one-pixel-wide skeletons follow diagonals. Differences show corners small protrusions: Guo-Hall K3M tend preserve corners marginally better Zhang-Suen; Lee tends toward thinner skeletons four directional sub-iterations process boundaries aggressively.

title: Choosing a thinning method
text: zhang_suen — default. predictable behavior. Use general purpose thinning compatibility code previously used EBImage::thinImage(). guo_hall — try skeletons lots diagonal features Zhang-Suen breaking corners. Slightly different topology preservation behavior. lee — want directional processing (four sub-iterations per pass, one per cardinal direction). Sometimes produces cleaner skeletons asymmetric inputs Zhang-Suen’s two-subiteration approach. k3m — strongest corner preservation published comparative studies, cost slower (six phases per outer iteration vs. two Zhang-Suen).

title: Choosing a thinning method
text: thin() accepts logical, integer, numeric matrices. Non-zero values foreground. return matrix matches storage mode input — logical , logical ; integer , integer ; numeric , numeric . Higher-dimensional arrays (e.g. 3-D volumes) yet supported. Lee algorithm v0.2 add 3-D support.

title: Choosing a thinning method
text: simple bench::mark() comparison moderate image (illustrative — see tests/testthat/test-thin.R test corpus basis benchmark report committed alongside release): four algorithms O(iterations × pixels). Constant factors increase roughly: zhang_suen < guo_hall < lee < k3m. 200×200 images four finish milliseconds modern hardware.
code: library(bench) m <- matrix(0L, 200, 200) m[50:150, 50:150] <- 1L  # solid square  bench::mark(   zs = thin(m, method = "zhang_suen"),   gh = thin(m, method = "guo_hall"),   iterations = 5,   check = FALSE )

title: Choosing a thinning method
text: Zhang, T. Y. & Suen, C. Y. (1984). fast parallel algorithm thinning digital patterns. Communications ACM, 27(3), 236–239. Guo, Z. & Hall, R. W. (1989). Parallel thinning two-subiteration algorithms. Communications ACM, 32(3), 359–373. Lee, T.-C., Kashyap, R. L., & Chu, C.-N. (1994). Building skeleton models via 3-D medial surface axis thinning algorithms. CVGIP: Graphical Models Image Processing, 56(6), 462–478. Saeed, K., Tabędzki, M., Rybnik, M., & Adamski, M. (2010). K3M: universal algorithm image skeletonization review thinning techniques. International Journal Applied Mathematics Computer Science, 20(2), 317–335.

title: thinr 0.2.0
text: lee — 2-D adaptation Lee, Kashyap & Chu (1994). Four directional sub-iterations (N / E / S / W boundary) crossing-number Euler-invariance check endpoint preservation. k3m — Saeed et al. (2010). Six-phase iterative thinning: phases 1–5 remove border pixels progressively permissive lookup tables, plus final phase 0 cleanup sweep strictest table. Includes crossing-number topology guard endpoint preservation.
